issues.legal_issue: The extension of a national succession law to a territory, together with express repeal of a corresponding local succession law, displaces the local law for the succession matters covered by the extended law.
material_facts: Before the territory became part of a larger state, a local statute governed intestate succession among Indian Christians there.
A later parliamentary statute extended the Indian Succession Act to the larger state, including the territory, and provided for repeal of local laws corresponding to the extended Acts.
The local statute and Chapter II of Part V of the Indian Succession Act covered the same subject matter: intestate succession among Indian Christians.
issues.conclusion: The local succession statute stood repealed, and intestate succession among Indian Christians in the territory was thereafter governed by Chapter II of Part V of the Indian Succession Act.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3 and 6 of the Part-B States (Laws) Act, 1951, the Indian Succession Act, 1925 was extended to the territory and a local law corresponding to an extended Act stood repealed. A local law corresponding to a chapter of the extended Act is repealed as to that subject even if the extended Act has broader coverage. The Court relied on Solomon v. Muthiah and noted that D. Chelliah v. G. Lalita Bai accepted that the local statute corresponded to Part V of the Indian Succession Act.

rule.if: intestate_succession_case and national_law_extended_to_territory and local_law_covers_same_succession_subject and extension_framework_repeals_corresponding_local_law

predicates.intestate_succession_case: The proceeding concerns who succeeds to property when a person dies without a will.
predicates.national_law_extended_to_territory: A national succession law was made applicable to the territory by a later enactment.
predicates.local_law_covers_same_succession_subject: A local law in force in the territory governed the same kind of intestate succession covered by the extended law.
predicates.extension_framework_repeals_correspondin: The enactment extending the national law provides that a local law corresponding to an extended law is repealed.

issues.definition: When an intestate-succession case concerns a territory where a national law has been extended to cover the same subject as a local law, and the extension framework repeals corresponding local laws, the extended succession law governs.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory provision that qualifies the application of succession rules does not incorporate a local succession law by reference or preserve that law after its express repeal.
material_facts: The local succession statute governed intestate succession among Indian Christians in the territory before the national law was extended there.
The local statute was expressly repealed under the enactment extending the national law.
The respondents argued that language in the national succession statute preserved or incorporated the local law.
The Court construed that language as a qualifying or excepting provision, rather than as a provision incorporating another statute by reference.
issues.conclusion: The relevant provision of the Indian Succession Act did not save the repealed local statute or incorporate it by reference.
issues.legal_principle: Section 29(2) of the Indian Succession Act, 1925 is a qualifying or excepting provision, not a device for incorporation by reference. Incorporation by reference uses language that adopts provisions of another statute; section 29(2) did not do so. The Court distinguished Kurian Augusty v. Devasay Aley.

predicates.intestate_succession_case: The proceeding concerns who succeeds to property when a person dies without a will.
predicates.local_succession_law_expressly_repealed: An enactment expressly repealed the local law that had governed the succession matter.
predicates.succession_statute_uses_qualifying_excep: The succession statute's relevant language qualifies or excepts the application of its rules rather than adopting the text of another statute.

issues.definition: If a local succession law has been expressly repealed and the applicable succession statute uses qualifying exception language, the local law is not saved through incorporation by reference.
